search_lead.cognate: ON bani 'slayer' (*gʷʰon-) ~ Ved. han- (*gʷʰen-); the slab sentence itself is fully renewed (vá < vega *weyk-, ormr < *wr̥mis)
search_lead.argument: Sigurðr vá orminn 'Sigurðr slew the serpent' continues HERO SLAY SERPENT with both words renewed. The verb root survives in the Edda epithet bani Fáfnis, which matches Ved. áhan áhim.

near_miss.lead: Sigurðr vá orminn ~ ahan vṛtraṃ / ahiḥ śayata (AVP line = RV 1.32.5c)
near_miss.why_not: Neither anchor shares a cognate with the other (vega vs han-, ormr vs ahi), and ahan is only in the AVP context line. Sent as a search lead with the bani Fáfnis witnesses.

cognate: ON var/váru (preterite of vesa < *h₂wes-) ~ Gk ἰαύω/ἄεσα (*h₂wes- 'spend the night'); ON nátt ~ Gk νύξ
drift_or_renewal: ON *h₂wes- has merged into the copula 'be', so the night-spending sense is no longer lexical; Indic renews the noun (rātriṃ vasati, uṣitvā)
shared_syntax: *h₂wes- verb + accusative of extent of 'night' (ON var um nóttina / váru þar aðra nótt; Gk ἀΰπνους νύκτας ἴαυον)
context: Close: King Óláfr spends the night awake at his prayers while the others are asleep; Achilles and Odysseus 'spent sleepless nights'. Both are a hero's sleepless night-vigil, and Greek and Indic tie *h₂wes- to spending the night. Weakness: in ON, 'be (somewhere) for the night' is everyday copula grammar, so chance is quite likely.

search_lead.cognate: ON fótr ~ OHG fuoz (*pṓds); horse word renewed (ON hestr vs OHG volo 'foal')
search_lead.argument: The king's horse falls while he rides and its feet are broken, and the king binds his horse's feet: the same scene as Merseburg II (the foot of Balder's foal is sprained while the gods ride and is healed by binding or joining limb to limb), whose healing formula matches AV 4.12. The ON is hagiography and its wording is not formulaic, so at most a Christianised reflex of the horse-healing theme.

near_miss.why_not: Generic simile; the partners (MBh snātām, ORu fire) do not share it.

near_miss.lead: allr heimrinn var mér fyrir augum (vision of the whole world)
near_miss.why_not: Christian vision topos; the partners only share 'big', 'eye' and 'be'.

near_miss.lead: hafði vegit mann hans ~ para-vīra-hā 'slayer of enemy heroes'
near_miss.why_not: Verbs not cognate (vega < *weyk- vs han-), maðr vs vīra not cognate, and the contexts differ.

near_miss.lead: hve marga menn hefir þú vegit í vígi (figura etymologica)
near_miss.why_not: Only inside ON; the ORu partner shares just *mon- and *weyd-.

near_miss.lead: liggja um nóttina ~ въ ту нощь лежащю ~ ἐλόχησαν ... νυκτός ('lie (in wait) at night')
near_miss.why_not: Cognate pair *legʰ- + *nókʷts, but collocates_8c shows night is not a distinctive collocate of *legʰ- in any branch. It is everyday 'lay overnight'.

near_miss.lead: of mjök er ort (poem composed) ~ ἔργα / kiuuerkôt
a woman identified as 'daughter of X, sister of Y' (dóttir ... systir ~ duhitā ... svasā)
near_miss.why_not: Cognate kin terms in apposition, but a genealogical pattern available to any language. The ON is prose genealogy and the AV a mythic personification.

near_miss.lead: idir fhir ⁊ mhnai ... idir ogh ⁊ shen (merisms 'men and women', 'young and old')
near_miss.why_not: Merisms only in the Irish. The ON shares kona/hundr by accident (hundr is a byname). A search for senos + young pairs finds only scattered generic hits.
Nothing shared beyond common vocabulary (the AVP partner is used in the dragon claim).

error.correct_reading: byname of Þórir hundr (part of a personal name)
vega 'fight, slay' < *weyk- only; *weǵʰ- belongs to vega 'weigh, carry'
error.evidence: context: Sigurðr vá orminn 'slew the serpent'
